rationale:
Evidence: iteration 9 (score 703.4) is nearly tied with iteration 8 (708.5). Oval (20/20) and s-bend (20/20) still complete reliably. Slalom is still 0/20 and ends off track at max_error about 0.063, just over the 0.06 m limit. Its progress rose from 0.56 (y=0.07) to 0.56 at y=0.08 with a small drop in s-bend and oval margin, so sensor look-ahead has reached diminishing returns. Mean rms_error on slalom is about 0.02, so the robot tracks on average and loses the line at sudden alternating bends. Raising kp was ruled out earlier (kp 3.7 hurt slalom and s-bend). Oval finishes in about 1.84 s and s-bend in about 2.09 s, so there is time margin under the 3.0 s cap.

Change (one variable): base_speed 1.3 to 1.1, with sensor y held at 0.08 m (iteration 9 geometry). Lower speed gives the correction more time at each bend and reduces lateral overshoot, which is the failure mode seen at max_error near the limit. Expected effect: slalom max_error falls below 0.06 more often and slalom progress rises; oval completion time rises to about 2.2 s and s-bend to about 2.4 s, still under 3.0 s. The time term in the score falls slightly, but completions should be more reliable. Hypotheses: (a) if slalom still exits at max_error near 0.06 with no progress gain, steering authority is the limit, so kp should move to about 3.3 with kd held. (b) If oval or s-bend completion falls below 20/20 or completion_time exceeds 2.8 s, base_speed is too low and should return to about 1.2. (c) If steering_oscillation rises above 0.35, kd should drop toward 0.6.
